MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  APRIL 17, 2023

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:03 p.m. at the City of Rolling Hills Estates Council
  Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR BAIN.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR BAIN led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina and
  Retz (arrived at 6:06 p.m.)

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  Also Present:  Mayor Britt Huff

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF MARCH
  20, 2023

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR
  MCCORMICK to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  MARCH 20, 2023.

  There being no objection, CHAIR BAIN so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
April 17, 2023
   A.  19TH AMENDMENT COMMEMORATION PLAQUE PROPOSAL

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  MAYOR HUFF presented her recommendation and gave a brief description and
  background information regarding the 19th Amendment commemoration plaque
  proposal.

  Linda Herman, Co-President of the Palos Verdes Peninsula League of Women
  Voters, gave additional background information and recommended the
  Commission approve the plaque.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if there would be a large-scale event. MAYOR
  HUFF noted that an event is planned for Saturday, August 26 to unveil the plaque
  and invites would be extended to dignitaries across the South Bay area.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that the City should explore opportunities to
  promote these type of events at other City events to assist in the outreach to the
  community.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  TO RECOMMEND THE CITY COUNCIL REVIEW AND APPROVE THE
  PROPOSED PLAQUE AND LOCATION FOR INSTALLATION.

  AYES:  Persichina, Pope, Retz, Ciarolla, McCormick and Bain
  ABSENT:  None

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  TENNIS CLUB OPEN HOUSE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the Tennis Club Open House which
  included a description of the activities, the turnout and level of participation by the
  attendees and the overall success of the event.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the main goal of the Open House was to help
  promote the pickleball overlays and pickleball programming at the tennis club in
  response to COMMISSIONER POPE.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated the number of participants was around the capacity of
  what the four pickleball courts could handle, in response to COMMISSIONER
  POPE.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
April 17, 2023
   Coordinator Morrow stated that the Open House was a one-time event, but an
  additional pickleball drop-in open play on Saturday afternoons could be scheduled
  due to the popularity of the drop-in play portion of the Open House, in response to
  COMMISSIONER POPE.

  CHAIR BAIN stated that she was able to attend the event, participated in some of
  the activities, and felt that the Open House was well received, fun and engaging for
  all the participants.

  In response to COMMISIONER POPE, Supervisor Pinuelas clarified that the
  intention was to have it be a one-time event, but another Open House could be
  looked at if a need arose to promote a new aspect of the tennis club.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA suggested if there was an opportunity to have a
  pickleball tournament as a fundraiser for the Pepper Tree Foundation. Supervisor
  Pinuelas stated that it would be something the City could offer in the future but
  noted that at this time staff is currently at a capacity with special events offered
  throughout the year.

  B.  MAYOR’S RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow provided a brief update of the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride
  scheduled for Saturday, May 13. He stated that Staff was excited that the local
  Scouts will return to provide their Pancake Breakfast and explained how to
  purchase tickets for the breakfast. He also gave an overview of the marketing of
  the event.

  Coordinator Morrow stated that the local Scouts sell tickets to their family and
  friends so many in attendance of the breakfast would be from those sales including
  the riders in response to VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  CHAIR BAIN suggested having a specific area for the COMMISSION during the
  breakfast to be able to answer questions and provide information regarding
  upcoming events and activities. Supervisor Pinuelas stated volunteers would be
  needed and asked what time would be best. It was determined that a 9:00 am –
  11:00 am time slot could work if there is an availability of COMMISSIONERS on
  that day.

  C.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
April 17, 2023
   A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK noted that when he was at Highridge Park he noticed
  water from the sprinklers was continuously running. Superintendent Goldsmith
  stated that he was aware of the issue and that one of the valves was stuck and that
  the issue has now been repaired.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK stated there was some erosion on the top part of the
  trail at George F Canyon as well as some poison oak, some overgrown branches,
  and the narrowing of the trail at some points due to some overgrowth.
  Superintendent Goldsmith stated these items are on the Maintenance project list
  for completion.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA asked about the west side of Chandler Preserve and
  if the City was going to remove the weeds and overgrowth along the trails.
  Superintendent Goldsmith stated trimming and removal of the weeds and
  overgrowth is scheduled to be completed.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK stated that while he was at Highridge Park he observed
  close to 20 dogs off leash along the center of the field that appeared to be a meet
  up of people at the park. He suggested the possibility of looking into a dog park
  somewhere in the City. Superintendent Goldsmith and Supervisor Pinuelas stated
  that they would send code enforcement to the park to inform people of the leash
  law.

  CHAIR BAIN asked if there was signage regarding leashes at the park.
  Superintendent Goldsmith stated he would verify that signs were postedand look
  into the possibility of adding more signs, if necessary.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked about the debris along the walking path
  around Field B at Ernie Howlett Park. Superintendent Goldsmith indicated that the
  area is planned to be cleaned soon. COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA also asked
  about the Silver Spur Little League scoreboard for Field B and if there was any
  update on its installation. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the Little League person
  in charge of the installation was not available and that Staff would follow up.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTION OF FEBRUARY 28, 2023

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
April 17, 2023
   RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  PUBLIC PARK OUTREACH

  11.  PARK TOURS

  A.  CHANDLER PARK, PEPPERWOOD PARK, ROCKBLUFF PARK, SILVER SPUR
  PARK

  Superintendent Goldsmith gave an overview of the maintenance of the gopher
  control at Chandler Park. He also noted the replacement of some of the fencing
  around the park and that it was intended to be a local Scout project, but the City
  has not received any interest lately.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK asked about the day-to-day use of the park.
  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that there was a small neighborhood yoga
  group that used the park. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA stated that she had noticed
  dog training . Supervisor Pinuelas stated that dog training is not allowed at the park
  and that code enforcement could be called to speak to those users as dog training
  is only approved at the equestrian grass area at Ernie Howlett Park.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the Chandler Park playground assessment is
  currently on hold in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK asked about the pipe project by George F Canyon and
  if they were going to regrade the area. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that it
  would be returned to the way it was prior to the start of the project.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that they have redone the footing and installed
  new gates and extended the handle, in response to COMMISSIONER POPE.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION WALKED TO PEPPERWOOD PARK FOR
  A TOUR**

  Superintendent Goldsmith gave a brief overview of Pepperwood Park and current
  maintenance projects.

  CHAIR BAIN asked if the grass area near the gazebo would be a good space for a
  dog park. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that it is too close to the horse
  arena for it to be a proper location for a dog park.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
April 17, 2023
   COMMISSIONER POPE asked about the use of the horse arena. Superintendent
  Goldsmith stated the arena is used frequently and is only one of two arenas in the
  City that is always open rain or shine.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION WENT TO ROCKBLUFF PARK FOR A
  TOUR**

  Superintendent Goldsmith gave a brief overview of the updates to the playground
  and ADA ramp at Rockbluff Park and noted the project should be completed soon.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA suggested placing a picnic bench in the grass
  area next to the new playground. Superintendent Goldsmith noted it would need to
  be one of the concrete benches due to the possibility of a lighter aluminum one
  being pushed down the hill.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION DECIDED TO NOT TOUR SILVER SPUR
  PARK**

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  CIAROLLA TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:19 PM TO THE NEXT PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MEETING ON MAY 15, 2023, AT 6:00 P.M., WHICH WILL BE
  HELD AT THE GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER AND PRESERVE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR BAIN so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Matt Morrow  Judy Bain
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
April 17, 2023
